1.explanation: All of the visual logic for invalid styling and icon placement lives in the Select component itself (the forwardRef function in Select.js). That function computes the wrapper CSS classes (including `${prefix}--select--invalid`), builds the `<select>` plus the icon markup in the `input` arrow function, and defines PropTypes for `invalid` and `invalidText`. To add a warning state you must extend this same component: add new props (e.g. `warn` and `warnText`) to Select.propTypes, adjust the classNames call to include a `${prefix}--select--warn` modifier when `warn` is true, and update the `input` builder to render the WarningFilled16 icon with the correct support-03 color and spacing when `warn` is passed. You’ll also need to update the story (Select-story.js) to expose the new prop and update tests in Select-test.js to assert the warning styling and markup.
1.bug_scenario: The design calls for a new “warning” state in the Select component—separate from the existing invalid (error) state—where a warning icon (WarningFilled16) is rendered in support-03 color, with specific spacing (16px left margin from the right edge, 8px between the icon and the dropdown arrow) and a warning message below the field. The screenshots show the desired yellow/black icon treatment and layout. Currently, Select only supports an `invalid` prop and renders the warning icon only in the error style, so the “warning” presentation and related props are missing.

2.explanation:
All of the identified class and function entries are central to how the Select component applies state, icons, text, and styling for validation. 
• Select (forwardRef) – the main component where new warning props must be accepted and routed into state.
• selectClasses – builds the CSS classes (currently only handles light, inline, disabled, invalid) and will need to include a ‘warning’ class.
• input arrow function – is where the invalid icon (<WarningFilled16 className=‘…__invalid-icon’/>) is rendered; that logic needs to be extended to render a separate warning icon when warning=true.
• error (the invalid message renderer) – only generates the invalidText message; a parallel warning renderer must be added.
• Select.propTypes & Select.defaultProps – currently define invalid and invalidText props; new propTypes (e.g. warning, warningText) and defaults must be declared so the component API supports the warning state.
2.bug_scenario: The user needs the <Select> component to support a new “warning” state (in addition to the existing “invalid” state). The screenshots show that when a “warning” prop is passed, the select box should render a yellow warning icon (WarningFilled16 in support-03), spaced 16px from the right edge of the input with 8px vertical alignment, and display a warning message underneath in the same styling as invalidText currently does. Right now, the component only supports an “invalid” state and renders the warning icon and message only when invalid is true.
